(3) Conflicting evidence—different string theory formulations (Type I, IIA, IIB, heterotic, M-theory) make different predictions, and papers disagree on whether any version qualifies as a true ToE given issues like landscape problem, non-falsifiability, lack of quantum gravity experiments. Resumen de la cuestión
La teoría de cuerdas es frecuentemente llamada la candidata privilegiada para una teoría del todo (TOE) por su capacidad teórica de integrar la gravedad cuántica con las interacciones gauge del Modelo Estándar en un marco consistente, junto con respaldos indirectos sólidos en física de agujeros negros y dualidades holográficas; sin embargo, también es criticada por depender de escenarios (p. ej. el multiverso y vacuos de alta energía) que harían sus predicciones poco o nunca verificables experimentalmente en el corto plazo, movilizando disputas filosóficas sobre si sigue siendo “ciencia” en el sentido falsacionista tradicional. <cite id="63024a63-1">String theory starts from quantum fields and implements the generalization from point particles to extended objects, leading to a more complete description of unification physics, though the unification picture is complicated by spacetime and the search for a more fundamental (M-)theory</cite> <cite id="61484266-0">Some prominent physicists have argued that certain proposed tests probe aspects of string theory or supergravity indirectly, and media hype around such proposals has fueled criticism about “theory of everything” claims</cite>.

¿Por qué se la considera la candidata más prometedora?
1) Unificación coherente de gravedad y gauge
La teoría de cuerdas ofrece un marco donde las partículas aparecen como estados cuánticos de cuerdas vibrantes y las interacciones derivan de su dinámica en una variedad espacio-temporal, integrando así la gravedad (a través de la relatividad general en el límite débil) con las fuerzas de gauge en una misma descripción cuántica. Esto contrasta con enfoques alternativos como la gravedad cuántica de bucles, que parten de la cuantización de la gravedad pero no incorporan fácilmente la materia; la teoría de cuerdas, por su estructura conforme y supersimetría, permite una “unificación más completa” a costa de complejidad y una búsqueda de una teoría más fundamental (M-theory) donde siquiera el propio espacio-tiempo emergiera de un estado vacío particular. <cite id="63024a63-2">String theory provides a viable framework to probe the unification of gravity and gauge interactions, with a multitude of consistent four-dimensional vacuum solutions whose selection is a central issue</cite> <cite id="63024a63-1">String theory starts from quantum fields and implements the generalization from point particles to extended objects, leading to discrete spectra and a more complete description of unification physics, but spacetime itself may emerge from a specific vacuum, motivating M-theory</cite>.

2) Predicción y explicación de fenómenos críticos: agujeros negros y dualidades
Un soporte indirecto decisivo es la reproducción estadística-mecánica de la entropía de agujeros negros extremales y casi-extremales, derivando expresiones complejas que antes solo se tenían en aproximaciones semiclásicas. Esto implica que la entropía de agujero negro tiene una origen estadístico y que la teoría de cuerdas es una ultracompleción ultravioleta de la relatividad general en los regímenes relevantes. Además, la física de agujeros negros motiva y guía la conjetura AdS/CFT entre gravedad en espacios anti-de Sitter y CFT en su frontera; AdS/CFT a su vez proporciona evidencia que trasciende el caso extremal, permitiendo estudios de dinámica, correcciones y propiedades termódinámicas. <cite id="f98cff13-0">String theory exactly reproduces the statistical-mechanical description of a large class of extremal and near-extremal black holes, deriving complicated semiclassical expressions for entropy and evaporation rates; this strongly suggests (a) a statistical-mechanical origin of black hole entropy and (b) string theory as an ultraviolet completion of quantum gravity in those regimes</cite> <cite id="f98cff13-0">The string-theoretic analysis of extremal black holes was a major motivation for the AdS/CFT duality, and AdS/CFT provides evidence for black hole statistical mechanics beyond the extremal case</cite> <cite id="f98cff13-1">AdS/CFT methods have been extended to rotating black holes and related settings, revealing nonperturbative stringy exclusion principles and connections to BTZ geometries, with studies of perturbations and corrections</cite>.

3) Alineación con el Modelo Estándar y “genéricidad” del nuestro
Desde la perspectiva fenomenológica, los datos de colisionadores respaldan el Modelo Estándar y su compatibilidad con una Gran Unificación (p. ej. SO(10)), mientras que muchos parámetros del Modelo Estándar aparecen como variables en GUTs pero carecen de explicación en teorías cuánticas de campos puntoales. Esto motiva explorar su origen dentro de una unificación con gravedad, donde la teoría de cuerdas constituye un único marco para estudiar cómo los parámetros estandar podrían surgir de una compactificación y branas. Por otra parte, la existencia de “múltiples vacíos” compatibles con observaciones permite plantear que nuestro universo corresponde a un punto en un espacio de vacíos posibles, una idea que atrae y critica por igual: por un lado, plantea una vía para entender la “genéricidad” del nuestro; por otro, atrae a quienes consideran que los otros universos postulados por el multiverso serían inobservables. <cite id="63024a63-2">The Standard Model data is compatible with renormalizable SM physics up to high scales and embedding in GUTs; unifying SM parameters with gravity suggests string theory as a unique framework to explore how SM parameters may arise</cite> <cite id="61484266-2">Some physicists argue string theory is testable in principle, yet concepts like the multiverse are troubling because other universes may be unobservable, making the enterprise heuristic for the foreseeable future</cite>.

4) “Testabilidad en principio” y estrategias de confrontación
Aunque la gravedad cuántica directa escapa a energías inaccesibles, la comunidad sostiene que la teoría de cuerdas es falsable en principio: por vías de alta energía (colisionadores o radiación gravitacional) y cosmología (inflación, anisotropías, dinámica de vacíos), o por aplicaciones emergentes en informática cuántica o materia condensada donde las estructuras conformales y superconformes “stringy” surjan indirectamente. Esto contrasta con la postura filosófica opuesta de que la ausencia de principios falsacionistas y la dependencia del multiverso la empujan hacia lo metafísico; sin embargo, debates en filosofía de la ciencia destacan que el límite práctico no es sinónimo de falta de testabilidad conceptual. <cite id="61484266-0">String theory has been criticized as a “theory of everything” test, yet proponents distinguish that some tests probe quantum information aspects or supergravity limits rather than the full TOE; media misinterpretations have fueled perceptions of hype, while experts acknowledge the limitation of such tests</cite> <cite id="61484266-2">There is a serious debate about whether string physics remains “science”; some argue it is testable in principle, while the multiverse aspect is seen as problematic due to inobservability of other universes, making it heuristic rather than empirically testable in the near term</cite>.

¿Por qué también se la critica por ser posible no verificable empíricamente?
1) Escalas energéticas inaccesibles y huellas difusas
Las predicciones clave (p. ej., resonancias de gravedad, agujeros de gusano, ondas gravitacionales cuánticas) operan cerca del Planck (~10^19 GeV), por debajo de cualquier acelerador real; las observaciones actuales en colisionadores y cosmología no destruyen el espacio de vacíos de la teoría, lo cual alimenta objeciones de que su contenido empírico es tan difuso como el de un “programa” matemático más que de una teoría empíricamente determinada. Esto motiva alternativas que buscan principios de selección de vacíos (p. ej., “swampland”) o estrategias de confrontación indirecta (p. ej., predicciones sobre inflación). <cite id="61484266-2">It will be possible to develop instruments to test string theory, but not in the foreseeable future; in the meantime it has a heuristic character</cite> <cite id="61484266-0">Famous critics have claimed specific tests do not prove the “theory of everything,” and some argued they do not even test string theory per se, highlighting the gap between proposed tests and direct confirmation of a TOE</cite>.

2) Multiverso y predicciones cosmológicas ambiguas
La posibilidad de que el nuestro sea solo un universo en una “mansarda” (landscape) plantea que universos vecinos difieran en constantes o campos inflacionarios, debilitando la posibilidad de predicciones compartidas. Esto ha impulsado críticas al “no-go” y al “maligno multiverso,” y motivado propuestas como la “cosmología predictiva del swampland” que busquen condiciones que separan teorías compatibles con gravedad cuántica de aquellas que no lo son; sin embargo, hay debate abierto sobre si estas condiciones son legítimas, empíricamente distinguibles o solo metafórmulas. <cite id="61484266-2">The multiverse aspect is troubling because other universes may be unobservable, undermining testability and pushing string theory toward heuristic/metaphysical status</cite> <cite id="61484266-0">Debates over whether proposed tests actually probe string theory or only low-energy limits (supergravity) illustrate the ambiguity of cosmological and high-energy signatures</cite>.

3) Filosofía de la ciencia: falsabilidad, underdetermination y reconceptualización metodológica
Críticos señalan que la teoría de cuerdas abandona el Popperismo tradicional: carece de principios de falsación directa claros y su éxito matemático/teórico puede valorarse sin datos, lo que la acerca a construcciones heurísticas o algorítmicas propuestas en filosofía de la ciencia. Esto se intensifica si se acepta el multiverso; por el contrario, defensores argumentan que la “verificabilidad en principio” (por detectores de gravedad, energía cuántica extrema o emergencia de estructuras stringy en nuevos contextos) preserva su estatus científico, si bien con horizontes temporales muy alejados. <cite id="61484266-1">String theories have shortcomings such as unclear principles, ambiguous and untestable predictions, mathematical complexity, and weak relation to experimentation; some physicists (e.g., Dawid) argue Bayesian reasoning is being misused by privileging internal consistency over data, fueling debates about whether string physics is “science”</cite> <cite id="61484266-2">There is a serious debate about testability/falsifiability; some see string theory as testable in principle, while the multiverse’s inobservability makes it heuristic in practice</cite>.

4) Hype, divergencias internas y disputas públicas
Eventos como anuncios apresurados de “pruebas” de la teoría de cuerdas o de “entrelazamiento cuántico” como test directo han amplificado percepciones de exceso de ambición o falta de rigor empírico, a pesar de que expertos distingan entre afirmaciones fuertes (prueba de una TOE) y afirmaciones más moderadas (validación de fragmentos o límites de la teoría). Esto refleja una comunidad en crisis de comunicación y en tensión interna sobre cómo calibrar el equilibrio entre matemática creativa y confrontación empírica. <cite id="61484266-0">High-profile media headlines have conflated string theory with a proven “theory of everything,” while experts clarify such tests do not establish a TOE and may target substructures (e.g., supergravity) rather than the full theory</cite>.

Síntesis: cómo coexisten ambas visiones
La teoría de cuerdas reúne elementos de una TOE prometedora: unifica coherente teóricamente gravedad y gauge, reproduce fenómenos críticos en agujeros negros, y ofrece una “arquitectura” para reconciliar el Modelo Estándar con gravedad cuántica a través de vacíos y compactificaciones; sin embargo, su contenido empírico clave opera en regímenes inaccesibles hoy, y su evolución hacia el multiverso y M-theory complica la falsación directa, arrastrando críticas filosóficas sobre si sigue siendo científica. La comunidad mantiene que la “verificabilidad en principio” subsiste (por cosmología, alta energía o emergencia indirecta), mientras que otros consideran que el edificio se desestabiliza por la pérdida de falsabilidad clara y la inobservabilidad de otros universos. Lo que resolvería las tensiones serían (i) límites de energía que aborden directamente modos stringy o (ii) principios de selección de vacíos robustos y empíricamente distinguibles que reduzcan el landscape a predicciones compartidas; hasta allí, el debate refleja una tensión legítima entre ambición explicativa y exigencia empírica. <cite id="63024a63-2">String theory provides a viable framework to probe unification, yet selecting the relevant four-dimensional vacua is a perplexing issue</cite> <cite id="f98cff13-0">String-theoretic black hole entropy reproductions support both a statistical origin of BH entropy and stringy ultraviolet completion in relevant regimes</cite> <cite id="61484266-2">String theory is argued to be testable in principle but heuristic due to inobservability of multiverse sectors in the foreseeable future</cite> <cite id="61484266-1">There is a serious debate about whether string physics remains science given unclear principles, ambiguous predictions, and weak relation to experimentation</cite>.

Guía práctica por temas y fuentes clave
- Unificación y microestados: <cite id="63024a63-1">Generalization from point particles to strings and the search for M-theory underpin unification</cite> <cite id="f98cff13-0">Exact reproduction of black hole entropy within string theory</cite>.
- Fenomenología y SM: <cite id="63024a63-2">Compatibility of SM data with GUT and motivation to embed SM parameters in a unified framework</cite>.
- Testabilidad en principio vs. inaccesibilidad: <cite id="61484266-2">Testable in principle but heuristic due to distant detectability and multiverse inobservability</cite> <cite id="61484266-0">Clarification that some proposed tests do not establish a TOE and may only probe substructures</cite>.
- Críticas filosóficas: <cite id="61484266-1">Ambiguous/ untestable predictions and weakened relation to experimentation fuel debates about whether string theory is science</cite>.
- Cosmología y landscape: <cite id="61484266-2">Multiverse observability issues challenge testability</cite> <cite id="61484266-0">Tensions between proposed tests and full TOE status</cite>.

Puntos abiertos y cómo evolucionarán las opiniones
La confrontación directa dependerá de: (i) avances en gravedad cuántica experimental (p. ej., detectores de ondas gravitacionales de alta frecuencia, resonancias gravitatorias) y (ii) claridad sobre principios de selección de vacíos que conviertan el landscape en predicciones falsables. Mientras tanto, la evidencia indirecta de agujeros negros y dualidades holográficas seguirá fortaleciendo el caso teórico, mientras que objeciones filosóficas y críticas a la predictibilidad de ciertos escenarios cosmológicos marcarán límites razonables a la ambición literal de “pruebas” próximas. <cite id="f98cff13-0">String-theoretic evidence for black hole statistical mechanics provides robust indirect support</cite> <cite id="61484266-2">Testability remains heuristic in practice, with some hope for future instrumentation but not in the near term</cite>.

On the other side, string theory starts from the quantum fields and implements the generalization from point particles to extended particles, like a one dimensional string or the higher dimensional branes. Snippet: String theory provides a viable framework to probe the unification of gravity and the gauge interactions. Preservation of classical symmetries in the quantised string fixes the number of world-sheet degrees of freedom required for internal consistency. These can be taken as bosonic degrees of freedom and interpreted as additional dimensions, beyond the four space-time, or as an internal two dimensional conformal field theory on the string world-sheet. String states are obtained by acting on the nondegenerate vacuum with bosonic and fermionic excitations and give rise to the matter and interaction states that constitute the experimentally observed spectrum. String theory in four dimensions gives rise to a multitude of consistent vacuum solutions and the selection of the ones relevant for experimental investigation is one of the perplexing issues in string theory. 

On the other hand, the data extracted from collider and other contemporary experiments highlights the Standard Particle Model as the correct accounting of all the observed data. Furthermore, the particle physics data is compatible with the hypothesis that the renormalisable Standard Model remains unaltered up to a large energy scale and that the particle spectrum is embedded in a Grand Unified Theory (GUT) [1]. Most appealing in this context is SO (10) unification, in which each Standard Model generation is embedded in a single 16 spinorial representation. The hypothesis of unification is further supported by the observed logarithmic evolution of the Standard Model parameters, by the suggestive compatibility of coupling unification with the low energy data and by the suppression of proton decay mediating operators and left-handed neutrino masses. However, as many of the Standard Model variables are mere parameters in the context of GUTs, their origin is not explained in the framework of point quantum field theories. Therefore, elucidating further the properties of the Standard Model spectrum, such as the existence of flavour, necessitates the unification of the Standard Particle Model with gravity. String theory therefore provides a unique framework to explore how the Standard Model parameters may arise from such unification. 

Toward this end and lacking a mechanism that dynamically selects a unique string vacuum in four dimensions, the Standard Model data is used to single out phenomenologically viable string vacua.

Title: The case for black hole thermodynamics part II: Statistical mechanics
Snippet: String theory exactly reproduces the statistical-mechanical description of a large class of extremal and near-extremal black holes, allowing us to derive by statisticalmechanical methods the highly complicated expressions for black hole entropy and evaporation rates that can be derived semiclassically via QFT on curved spacetime, It is pretty difficult to explain this reproduction without accepting that (a) black hole entropy has a statistical-mechanical origin; (b) string theory provides an ultraviolet completion of low-energy quantum general relativity in at least the regimes appropriate to those black holes. 

The string-theoretic analysis of extremal black holes was also a major motivation and precursor for the conjectured duality (Maldacena 1998, Gubser, Klebanov, and Polyakov 1998, Witten 1998) between quantum gravity on anti-de Sitter (AdS) space and conformal quantum field theory (CFT) on the boundary of that space (indeed, in current presentations, the leading-order terms in those calculations are normally reinterpreted in terms of that duality.) But AdS/CFT duality provides evidence for BHSM that goes well beyond the extremal case; in this section I give a brief introduction to AdS/CFT and then consider, in sequence, the evidence for AdS/CFT itself and the evidence it provides for BHSM. 

For more details on AdS/CFT see review articles by Aharony et al (1999), Harlow (2016), Hartman (2015), and Kaplan (2016) (my account here is based on these sources, especially Harlow and Kaplan). For philosophical discussion, see, e. g. , De Haro, Mayerson, and Butterfield (2016) or Teh (2013).

Title: TOPICAL REVIEW: The Bekenstein formula and string theory (N-brane theory)
Snippet: New methods for computing the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy of black holes have been investigated since the AdS/CFT correspondence [97] came to light.

We have seen that five-dimensional black holes can be thought of as six-dimensional black strings compactified on a circle. The near-horizon geometry of the black strings turns out to be AdS 3 × S 3 . More precisely, the first factor is a BTZ black hole, which is everywhere locally (but not globally) AdS 3 . A new counting of black hole entropy was done in [249]. (Although the counting was probably motivated by the stringy AdS/CFT correspondence, the method used was actually independent of it.) String theory on AdS 3 is dual to a d = 1+1 CFT, and the isometry group is infinite-dimensional. The entropy was computed using older results on the central charge of the CFT and using Cardy's formula to get the degeneracy of states. In this approach there were some technical subtleties, and unresolved issues such as the question of where the states being counted reside. The presence of holography makes localization in the radial coordinate of the AdS factor a tricky issue.

A lucent discussion of the subtleties in counting the entropy of the BTZ black hole via different methods, and additional references, may be found in a recent overview article by Carlip. We refer the interested reader to that work [250].

AdS/CFT methods were extended to rotating d = 5 black holes in [251], and the S-dual NS-NS case was studied in [252]. The BTZ factor was seen [253] in the d = 4 case by lifting on x ♮ to M-theory (the other factor being S 2 ), and d = 4 rotation was discussed in [254]. BPS states were tracked in [255], and a nonperturbative stringy exclusion principle was found to be operating. In that work it was also shown how the discrete identifications giving BTZ from AdS 3 give a natural mechanism for seeing thermal effects in the black hole background. The relation between AdS/CFT and perturbations of black holes was studied in e.g. [256]. Some corrections to leading-order results have been investigated in [257]

Title: AdS Holography and Strings on the Horizon
Snippet: The microscopic origin of black hole entropy remains one of the more intriguing open questions in theoretical physics. A subplot in this drama is the renowned Cardy-Verlinde formula, which uses two-dimensional conformal formalism to explain the entropy of an arbitrary-dimensional black hole. In this paper, by exploiting the AdS/CFT and black hole-string dualities, we are able to provide a physical picture for this paradoxical behavior. Following a recent study by Haylo (in a dS context), we show that the dual CFT for an asymptotically AdS spacetime actually conforms to a string-like description. Moreover, we demonstrate that this stringy CFT is directly related to a string that lives on the stretched horizon of an AdS-Schwarzschild-like black hole. In fact, after an appropriate renormalization, these two boundary theories are shown to be thermodynamically equivalent.

La teoría de cuerdas es frecuentemente llamada la candidata privilegiada para una teoría del todo (TOE) por su capacidad teórica de integrar la gravedad cuántica con las interacciones gauge del Modelo Estándar en un marco consistente, junto con respaldos indirectos sólidos en física de agujeros negros y dualidades holográficas; sin embargo, también es criticada por depender de escenarios (p. ej. el multiverso y vacuos de alta energía) que harían sus predicciones poco o nunca verificables experimentalmente en el corto plazo, movilizando disputas filosóficas sobre si sigue siendo “ciencia” en el sentido falsacionista tradicional. <cite id="63024a63-1">String theory starts from quantum fields and implements the generalization from point particles to extended objects, leading to a more complete description of unification physics, though the unification picture is complicated by spacetime and the search for a more fundamental (M-)theory</cite> <cite id="61484266-0">Some prominent physicists have argued that certain proposed tests probe aspects of string theory or supergravity indirectly, and media hype around such proposals has fueled criticism about “theory of everything” claims</cite>.

La teoría de cuerdas ofrece un marco donde las partículas aparecen como estados cuánticos de cuerdas vibrantes y las interacciones derivan de su dinámica en una variedad espacio-temporal, integrando así la gravedad (a través de la relatividad general en el límite débil) con las fuerzas de gauge en una misma descripción cuántica. Esto contrasta con enfoques alternativos como la gravedad cuántica de bucles, que parten de la cuantización de la gravedad pero no incorporan fácilmente la materia; la teoría de cuerdas, por su estructura conforme y supersimetría, permite una “unificación más completa” a costa de complejidad y una búsqueda de una teoría más fundamental (M-theory) donde siquiera el propio espacio-tiempo emergiera de un estado vacío particular. <cite id="63024a63-2">String theory provides a viable framework to probe the unification of gravity and gauge interactions, with a multitude of consistent four-dimensional vacuum solutions whose selection is a central issue</cite> <cite id="63024a63-1">String theory starts from quantum fields and implements the generalization from point particles to extended objects, leading to discrete spectra and a more complete description of unification physics, but spacetime itself may emerge from a specific vacuum, motivating M-theory</cite>.

2) Predicción y explicación de fenómenos críticos: agujeros negros y dualidades
Un soporte indirecto decisivo es la reproducción estadística-mecánica de la entropía de agujeros negros extremales y casi-extremales, derivando expresiones complejas que antes solo se tenían en aproximaciones semiclásicas. Esto implica que la entropía de agujero negro tiene una origen estadístico y que la teoría de cuerdas es una ultracompleción ultravioleta de la relatividad general en los regímenes relevantes. Además, la física de agujeros negros motiva y guía la conjetura AdS/CFT entre gravedad en espacios anti-de Sitter y CFT en su frontera; AdS/CFT a su vez proporciona evidencia que trasciende el caso extremal, permitiendo estudios de dinámica, correcciones y propiedades termódinámicas. <cite id="f98cff13-0">String theory exactly reproduces the statistical-mechanical description of a large class of extremal and near-extremal black holes, deriving complicated semiclassical expressions for entropy and evaporation rates; this strongly suggests (a) a statistical-mechanical origin of black hole entropy and (b) string theory as an ultraviolet completion of quantum gravity in those regimes</cite> <cite id="f98cff13-0">The string-theoretic analysis of extremal black holes was a major motivation for the AdS/CFT duality, and AdS/CFT provides evidence for black hole statistical mechanics beyond the extremal case</cite> <cite id="f98cff13-1">AdS/CFT methods have been extended to rotating black holes and related settings, revealing nonperturbative stringy exclusion principles and connections to BTZ geometries, with studies of perturbations and corrections</cite>.

Desde la perspectiva fenomenológica, los datos de colisionadores respaldan el Modelo Estándar y su compatibilidad con una Gran Unificación (p. ej. Aunque la gravedad cuántica directa escapa a energías inaccesibles, la comunidad sostiene que la teoría de cuerdas es falsable en principio: por vías de alta energía (colisionadores o radiación gravitacional) y cosmología (inflación, anisotropías, dinámica de vacíos), o por aplicaciones emergentes en informática cuántica o materia condensada donde las estructuras conformales y superconformes “stringy” surjan indirectamente. Críticos señalan que la teoría de cuerdas abandona el Popperismo tradicional: carece de principios de falsación directa claros y su éxito matemático/teórico puede valorarse sin datos, lo que la acerca a construcciones heurísticas o algorítmicas propuestas en filosofía de la ciencia. 4) Hype, divergencias internas y disputas públicas
Eventos como anuncios apresurados de “pruebas” de la teoría de cuerdas o de “entrelazamiento cuántico” como test directo han amplificado percepciones de exceso de ambición o falta de rigor empírico, a pesar de que expertos distingan entre afirmaciones fuertes (prueba de una TOE) y afirmaciones más moderadas (validación de fragmentos o límites de la teoría). Esto refleja una comunidad en crisis de comunicación y en tensión interna sobre cómo calibrar el equilibrio entre matemática creativa y confrontación empírica. <cite id="61484266-0">High-profile media headlines have conflated string theory with a proven “theory of everything,” while experts clarify such tests do not establish a TOE and may target substructures (e.g., supergravity) rather than the full theory</cite>.

- Unificación y microestados: <cite id="63024a63-1">Generalization from point particles to strings and the search for M-theory underpin unification</cite> <cite id="f98cff13-0">Exact reproduction of black hole entropy within string theory</cite>.

La confrontación directa dependerá de: (i) avances en gravedad cuántica experimental (p. ej., detectores de ondas gravitacionales de alta frecuencia, resonancias gravitatorias) y (ii) claridad sobre principios de selección de vacíos que conviertan el landscape en predicciones falsables. Title: Quantum gravity at the fifth root of unity
Snippet: Quantum gravity and unification physics programs, in the absence of more concrete experimental results, rely much on rigorous mathematical results to make progress. The old and well established quantum gravity programs of loop quantum gravity (LQG) [1] and string theory [2,3] are good examples of this new paradigm to find clues about the underlying physics at the Planck scale. For a review of the motivations and main results of LQG and spin foam models we recommend the book [1]. We also recommend a review of the main elements of the higher dimensional Lie algebra unification program [4,5,6,7,8], which is closely related to string theory. With those results as guides, this paper will construct a model that does not have a priori assumptions of general relativity (GR) and the usual Yang Mills gauge quantum fields, but yet has their building blocks arXiv:1903.10851v2 [hep-th] 15 Apr 2019 built-in in a consistent way to generate their emergent macroscopic properties starting only from the notion of quantum geometry. 

It is interesting to point out that LQG starts from GR and provides its quantization which leads to the quantization of the geometry itself; lengths, areas and volumes, in operator form, have discrete spectra; they have minimum quanta. But it does not incorporate matter and the quantum fields − the charge space symmetries. On the other side, string theory starts from the quantum fields and implements the generalization from point particles to extended particles, like a one dimensional string or the higher dimensional branes. This also leads to discrete spectra, and a more complete description of unification physics. But this unification picture is more complicated because the strings are defined over a spacetime manifold, which leads to fundamental problems and the search for a more fundamental (M −)theory, where one hopes to understand the existence of a spacetime manifold itself as the emergent property of a specific vacuum rather than an identifiable feature of the underlying theory [3]. A partner approach of string theory, but less ambitious, is the Lie algebraic unification program, as in E 8 unification [9,10].

Title: Minimal standard heterotic string models
Snippet: String theory provides a viable framework to probe the unification of gravity and the gauge interactions. Preservation of classical symmetries in the quantised string fixes the number of world-sheet degrees of freedom required for internal consistency. These can be taken as bosonic degrees of freedom and interpreted as additional dimensions, beyond the four space-time, or as an internal two dimensional conformal field theory on the string world-sheet. String states are obtained by acting on the nondegenerate vacuum with bosonic and fermionic excitations and give rise to the matter and interaction states that constitute the experimentally observed spectrum. String theory in four dimensions gives rise to a multitude of consistent vacuum solutions and the selection of the ones relevant for experimental investigation is one of the perplexing issues in string theory. 

On the other hand, the data extracted from collider and other contemporary experiments highlights the Standard Particle Model as the correct accounting of all the observed data. Furthermore, the particle physics data is compatible with the hypothesis that the renormalisable Standard Model remains unaltered up to a large energy scale and that the particle spectrum is embedded in a Grand Unified Theory (GUT) [1]. Most appealing in this context is SO (10) unification, in which each Standard Model generation is embedded in a single 16 spinorial representation. The hypothesis of unification is further supported by the observed logarithmic evolution of the Standard Model parameters, by the suggestive compatibility of coupling unification with the low energy data and by the suppression of proton decay mediating operators and left-handed neutrino masses. However, as many of the Standard Model variables are mere parameters in the context of GUTs, their origin is not explained in the framework of point quantum field theories. Therefore, elucidating further the properties of the Standard Model spectrum, such as the existence of flavour, necessitates the unification of the Standard Particle Model with gravity. String theory therefore provides a unique framework to explore how the Standard Model parameters may arise from such unification. 

Toward this end and lacking a mechanism that dynamically selects a unique string vacuum in four dimensions, the Standard Model data is used to single out phenomenologically viable string vacua.

Title: The case for black hole thermodynamics part II: Statistical mechanics
Snippet: String theory exactly reproduces the statistical-mechanical description of a large class of extremal and near-extremal black holes, allowing us to derive by statisticalmechanical methods the highly complicated expressions for black hole entropy and evaporation rates that can be derived semiclassically via QFT on curved spacetime, It is pretty difficult to explain this reproduction without accepting that (a) black hole entropy has a statistical-mechanical origin; (b) string theory provides an ultraviolet completion of low-energy quantum general relativity in at least the regimes appropriate to those black holes. 

The string-theoretic analysis of extremal black holes was also a major motivation and precursor for the conjectured duality (Maldacena 1998, Gubser, Klebanov, and Polyakov 1998, Witten 1998) between quantum gravity on anti-de Sitter (AdS) space and conformal quantum field theory (CFT) on the boundary of that space (indeed, in current presentations, the leading-order terms in those calculations are normally reinterpreted in terms of that duality.) But AdS/CFT duality provides evidence for BHSM that goes well beyond the extremal case; in this section I give a brief introduction to AdS/CFT and then consider, in sequence, the evidence for AdS/CFT itself and the evidence it provides for BHSM. 

For more details on AdS/CFT see review articles by Aharony et al (1999), Harlow (2016), Hartman (2015), and Kaplan (2016) (my account here is based on these sources, especially Harlow and Kaplan). For philosophical discussion, see, e. g. , De Haro, Mayerson, and Butterfield (2016) or Teh (2013).

Title: TOPICAL REVIEW: The Bekenstein formula and string theory (N-brane theory)
Snippet: New methods for computing the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy of black holes have been investigated since the AdS/CFT correspondence [97] came to light.

We have seen that five-dimensional black holes can be thought of as six-dimensional black strings compactified on a circle. The near-horizon geometry of the black strings turns out to be AdS 3 × S 3 . More precisely, the first factor is a BTZ black hole, which is everywhere locally (but not globally) AdS 3 . A new counting of black hole entropy was done in [249]. (Although the counting was probably motivated by the stringy AdS/CFT correspondence, the method used was actually independent of it.) String theory on AdS 3 is dual to a d = 1+1 CFT, and the isometry group is infinite-dimensional. The entropy was computed using older results on the central charge of the CFT and using Cardy's formula to get the degeneracy of states. In this approach there were some technical subtleties, and unresolved issues such as the question of where the states being counted reside. The presence of holography makes localization in the radial coordinate of the AdS factor a tricky issue.

A lucent discussion of the subtleties in counting the entropy of the BTZ black hole via different methods, and additional references, may be found in a recent overview article by Carlip. We refer the interested reader to that work [250].

AdS/CFT methods were extended to rotating d = 5 black holes in [251], and the S-dual NS-NS case was studied in [252]. The BTZ factor was seen [253] in the d = 4 case by lifting on x ♮ to M-theory (the other factor being S 2 ), and d = 4 rotation was discussed in [254]. BPS states were tracked in [255], and a nonperturbative stringy exclusion principle was found to be operating. In that work it was also shown how the discrete identifications giving BTZ from AdS 3 give a natural mechanism for seeing thermal effects in the black hole background. The relation between AdS/CFT and perturbations of black holes was studied in e.g. [256]. Some corrections to leading-order results have been investigated in [257]

Title: AdS Holography and Strings on the Horizon
Snippet: The microscopic origin of black hole entropy remains one of the more intriguing open questions in theoretical physics. A subplot in this drama is the renowned Cardy-Verlinde formula, which uses two-dimensional conformal formalism to explain the entropy of an arbitrary-dimensional black hole. In this paper, by exploiting the AdS/CFT and black hole-string dualities, we are able to provide a physical picture for this paradoxical behavior. Following a recent study by Haylo (in a dS context), we show that the dual CFT for an asymptotically AdS spacetime actually conforms to a string-like description. Moreover, we demonstrate that this stringy CFT is directly related to a string that lives on the stretched horizon of an AdS-Schwarzschild-like black hole. In fact, after an appropriate renormalization, these two boundary theories are shown to be thermodynamically equivalent.

documents.title: The case for black hole thermodynamics part II: Statistical mechanics
documents.snippet:
String theory exactly reproduces the statistical-mechanical description of a large class of extremal and near-extremal black holes, allowing us to derive by statisticalmechanical methods the highly complicated expressions for black hole entropy and evaporation rates that can be derived semiclassically via QFT on curved spacetime, It is pretty difficult to explain this reproduction without accepting that (a) black hole entropy has a statistical-mechanical origin; (b) string theory provides an ultraviolet completion of low-energy quantum general relativity in at least the regimes appropriate to those black holes. 

The string-theoretic analysis of extremal black holes was also a major motivation and precursor for the conjectured duality (Maldacena 1998, Gubser, Klebanov, and Polyakov 1998, Witten 1998) between quantum gravity on anti-de Sitter (AdS) space and conformal quantum field theory (CFT) on the boundary of that space (indeed, in current presentations, the leading-order terms in those calculations are normally reinterpreted in terms of that duality.) But AdS/CFT duality provides evidence for BHSM that goes well beyond the extremal case; in this section I give a brief introduction to AdS/CFT and then consider, in sequence, the evidence for AdS/CFT itself and the evidence it provides for BHSM. 

For more details on AdS/CFT see review articles by Aharony et al (1999), Harlow (2016), Hartman (2015), and Kaplan (2016) (my account here is based on these sources, especially Harlow and Kaplan). For philosophical discussion, see, e. g. , De Haro, Mayerson, and Butterfield (2016) or Teh (2013).

documents.title: TOPICAL REVIEW: The Bekenstein formula and string theory (N-brane theory)
documents.snippet:
New methods for computing the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy of black holes have been investigated since the AdS/CFT correspondence [97] came to light.

We have seen that five-dimensional black holes can be thought of as six-dimensional black strings compactified on a circle. The near-horizon geometry of the black strings turns out to be AdS 3 × S 3 . More precisely, the first factor is a BTZ black hole, which is everywhere locally (but not globally) AdS 3 . A new counting of black hole entropy was done in [249]. (Although the counting was probably motivated by the stringy AdS/CFT correspondence, the method used was actually independent of it.) String theory on AdS 3 is dual to a d = 1+1 CFT, and the isometry group is infinite-dimensional. The entropy was computed using older results on the central charge of the CFT and using Cardy's formula to get the degeneracy of states. In this approach there were some technical subtleties, and unresolved issues such as the question of where the states being counted reside. The presence of holography makes localization in the radial coordinate of the AdS factor a tricky issue.

A lucent discussion of the subtleties in counting the entropy of the BTZ black hole via different methods, and additional references, may be found in a recent overview article by Carlip. We refer the interested reader to that work [250].

AdS/CFT methods were extended to rotating d = 5 black holes in [251], and the S-dual NS-NS case was studied in [252]. The BTZ factor was seen [253] in the d = 4 case by lifting on x ♮ to M-theory (the other factor being S 2 ), and d = 4 rotation was discussed in [254]. BPS states were tracked in [255], and a nonperturbative stringy exclusion principle was found to be operating. In that work it was also shown how the discrete identifications giving BTZ from AdS 3 give a natural mechanism for seeing thermal effects in the black hole background. The relation between AdS/CFT and perturbations of black holes was studied in e.g. [256]. Some corrections to leading-order results have been investigated in [257]

Resumen de la pregunta
¿Cuáles diferencias predictivas permiten distinguir empíricamente a una “teoría del todo” (ToE) de la teoría de cuerdas en experimentos de colisionadores? La respuesta se basa en comparar predictores observables en canales definidos: escalas de energía, patrones de espín y resonancias, dinámica gravitacional y objetos cuánticos de string (tensores antisimétricos), y huellas de singularidades gravitationales como agujeros negros o “bolas de cuerda”. En los datos del LHC y en propuestas de colisionadores de energía más alta, ciertas anomalías en distribuciones dijet, resonancias cuánticas de cuerda, ausencia de desviaciones en regiones de parámetros, y patrones de energía/ángulo/missing E_T permiten rechazar o aceptar modelos string vs alternativos (GUT, extra dimensiones, etc.). <cite id="5e4b3b04-0">Existen expresiones concretas de correcciones “cuerda” que permiten buscar señales de la teoría de cuerdas en colisionadores</cite><cite id="5e4b3b04-3">Estudios detallados de construcciones string calculan observables LHC (“conteos”, “distribuciones”, E_T, invariant mass) y tabulan las combinaciones que las diferencian de otras construcciones o ToE no string</cite>.

1) Escalas de energía: contactos y “fondos” de string
En las teorías con gravedad a escalas accesibles, los colisionadores prueban dos capas de predicción: interacciones de contacto a energías por debajo de la escala fundamental y resonancias directas si la escala es baja. <cite id="5e4b3b04-0">Se pueden observar “contact interactions” incluso por debajo de la escala de cuerda, junto con observación directa de las excitaciones de Regge</cite><cite id="5e4b3b04-4">Con recientes evidencias, la energía asociada a efectos de cuerda puede ser significativamente más baja que la Planck o GUT, abriendo una ventana experimental</cite>. Esto distingue a los modelos string de alternativas cuya energía de nuevo físico es más alta o que carecen de tal espectro de “oscilaciones” cuánticas. Por contraparte, en escenarios gravitatorios de alta dimensión motivados por la teoría de cuerdas, <cite id="5e4b3b04-2">los canales de “missing energy” por emisión real de gravedad a dimensiones extra y las anomalías en pares de gauge/fermiones surgen como pruebas directas de escalas de Planck o string reducidas</cite>.

2) Resonancias de Regge: espín cuántico y “pasos” discretos en la masa
Un hallazgo distintivo de la teoría de cuerdas son las excitaciones de vibración (Regge) de partones colorados y gauge, con masas cuantizadas y espín máximo fijo; en colisionadores, esto deja huellas en distribuciones dijet y en procesos gauge-fermión que exceden el QCD puntual. <cite id="eb6a778e-0">Para procesos 2→2 con cuatro gauge bosones o dos gauge+dos fermiones, las amplitudes string determinan contribuciones dominantes cuyos polos s-canal son universales y independientes de detalles de compactificación</cite><cite id="eb6a778e-1">Esto permite extracción de “efectos genuinos de cuerda” que son independientes de cómo se compactan las dimensiones extra</cite>. <cite id="eb6a778e-3">La primera excitación del gluón tiene espín 2 y anchura del orden de 1/Ms, produciendo un pico característico en la producción dijet; las excitaciones de quarks tienen espín 3/2</cite><cite id="eb6a778e-2">Estos modos aparecen como resonancias en la distribución de masa invariante dijet, probables para Ms ~ TeV</cite>. <cite id="4a855975-0">Estas secciones de choque “cuerda” se obtienen a nivel árbol y reproducen el QCD a baja energía, mientras que términos de ordenes altos en α′ describen correcciones por intercambio de Reggeones</cite>. Esto contrasta con las predicciones de ToEs no string (p. ej., GUTs), donde las resonancias típicas surgen de partículas puntualmente cargadas (p. ej., X bosones) sin las “leyes de pasos” en m^2 ni los umbrales de producción universalmente spin-dependientes que caracterizan a las excitaciones de cuerda. <cite id="5e4b3b04-4">La presencia de tales resonancias, junto con partones adicionales ligeros, suele dificultar la separación “árbol vs bosque”, pero permiten identificar huellas string si se estudian amplitudes universales</cite>.

3) Dinámica gravitacional de baja energía: agujeros negros vs “bolas de cuerda”
La creación de singularidades gravitationales es un puente teórico entre ToEs: en cuerdas, los “string-balls” producidos a energías TeV decaen térmicamente, mientras que los agujeros negros relativistas generales requieren umbrales bien por encima del alcance LHC en el marco de las versiones perturbativas de TeV-string. <cite id="4a855975-1">En teoría de cuerdas débilmente acoplada, la energía de umbral para la producción de agujeros negros es mucho más alta que la energía de la cuerda y las Planck de alta dimensión, por lo que los “string balls” aparecen con altas tasas y decaen térmicamente, semejantes a agujeros negros pero distintos en su dinámica</cite><cite id="4a855975-0">En un marco de cuerda perturbativa a TeV, el umbral de producción de micro agujeros negros supera ampliamente el alcance LHC; la masa de un agujero negro d-dimensional depende de GN ~ gs y del tamaño de la cuerda</cite>. Esto distingue a los modelos string de predicciones de otras ToEs que permitan directamente agujeros negros primordiales o cuyas temperaturas de Hawking generen espectros característicos. Además, <cite id="4a855975-3">las correcciones cuánticas de string aparecen como términos de curvatura superior (p. ej., Gauss–Bonnet en heterótica), lo que deja huellas en geometrías de agujero negro de baja energía compatibles con colisionadores</cite>.

4) Señales de extra-dimensiones en el contexto string: KK gravitones vs KK gauge
La teoría de cuerdas incluye escenarios con dimensiones extra que predicen resonancias de Kaluza–Klein tanto para gravedad como para gauge; en colisionadores, estas se ven en canales específicos y permiten separar mecanismos. <cite id="5e4b3b04-2">Los dos escenarios típicos son: (i) gravedad libre en dimensiones extra (ADD) con señales de “missing energy” por emisión real de gravitones y aumen tos de produc ción por intercambio virtual; (ii) gauge bosones permitidos en extra-dimensiones (unificación de coupl ings por debajo de GUT) cuyas KK-states generan diphoton, pares de gauge y fermiones, y precision</cite>. <cite id="4a855975-2">La primera categoría (“missing energy”) surge por emisión real de gravitones en extra-dimensiones, mientras que la segunda (“KK gauge”) predice resonancias de fotones y gauge a energías más bajas, con una menor gravedad efectiva</cite>. Esto contrasta con ToEs alternativas sin dimensiones extra: sus predicciones de KK suelen ser de gauge solamente, o carecen de la dinámica de gravedad cuantizada que produce ahorcos de energía o resonancias de gravitones a escalas reducidas. <cite id="5e4b3b04-4">En string, además de tales resonancias, los modos adicional es (p. ej., gauge nuevos, sector Higgs extendido) entran en juego, lo cual complica la separación pero genera correlaciones entre resonancias gauge y gravitónicas</cite>.

5) Pruebas de objetos únicos de string: tensores antisimétricos y couplings gravitatorios característicos
Algunos componentes de la teoría de cuerdas son exclusivos y fáciles de probar: <cite id="5e4b3b04-2">los campos tensores antisimétricos son predicciones únicas de la teoría de cuerdas; con colisionadores, se buscan en procesos como Bhabha o Møller donde los canales de resonancia permiten poner límites rigurosos</cite>. Por ejemplo, los límites actuales de OPAL en √s ~130–136 GeV descartan masas de tensores menores de ~710 GeV para couplings compatibles con ausencia de resonancias en LHC, estableciendo una frontera operativa en experimentos futuros. Esto distingue a las construcciones string de ToEs alternativas que no predicen tal espectro fundamental. De igual modo, <cite id="eb6a778e-0">las amplitudes universales de intercambio de Reggeon permiten observar correlaciones gauge+fermión que no son reprodu cidas por teorías punto-partícula generales</cite>.

6) Supersimetría a la escala de cuerda y su discriminación
Muchas construcciones string predicen supersimetría cuyos sectores y soft-breaking couplings presentan correlaciones únicas al ser “deshojadas” hacia 4D. <cite id="5e4b3b04-3">Estudios de “string constructions” calculan Lagrangianas efectivas y sus observables LHC (conteos y distribuciones), identificando “señales útiles” que diferencian construcciones</cite>. Esto permite contrastar patrones de E_T, leptones, jets y mass-degeneraciones con los de ToEs alternativas (p. ej., supersimetría AMSB o GUT-embeddings), donde los correlatos de string (p. ej., multiplicidad de estados híbridos en D-branas, sector gauge adicional) dejan huellas diferenciadas en invariant mass y topología de eventos. <cite id="5e4b3b04-4">El “bosque” de partículas adicionales suele acompañar a los “árboles” de la física de string, por lo que los estudios modelos-dependientes son necesarios, pero se complementan con “patrones” universales en observables</cite>.

7) Resultados LHC y alcance de colisionadores futuros
Los datos del LHC ya restringen escenarios string-Regge y de baja escala de gravedad. <cite id="eb6a778e-0">CMS ha descartado Ms < 2.5 TeV con 2.9 pb−1 y luego extendió a Ms < 4 TeV con >1 fb−1, lo que impide ver las primeras excitaciones de Regge en dijet</cite><cite id="eb6a778e-2">Con ~170 pb−1 (7 TeV), el LHC puede probar Ms ≥3.5–5 TeV en dijet, y ya observó una anomalía en m_jj asociada a W que se explica con una escala de cuerda baja</cite>. Esto separa empíricamente a los modelos string sin ajustar sus parámetros: si no aparecen tales resonancias en regiones permitidas, se rechazan variantes de baja Ms. En el horizonte, <cite id="eb6a778e-1">el HL-LHC puede descubrir excitaciones de Regge hasta Ms ~7.1 TeV con 5σ en dijet y hasta ~15 TeV en HE-LHC/VLHC</cite><cite id="eb6a778e-0">La capacidad de descubrimiento de resonancias fuertemente interactuantes en dijet abarca casi hasta 1/2 √s_LHC</cite>. Por su parte, <cite id="4a855975-1">las “string balls” son más alcanzables que los agujeros negros relativistas generales en LHC, ofreciendo eventos con alta multiplicidad de jets y E_T y decaimientos térmicos distinguibles</cite>.

8) Síntesis: diferencias predictivas operativas en colisionadores
- Señales spin-2/3/2 discretos y resonancias en dijet: <cite id="eb6a778e-3">Picos en m_jj con espín 2/3/2 y pasos en m^2 ∼ 2 Ms (Regge), no observados en QCD puntual</cite>; <cite id="4a855975-0">amplitudes universales de string vs QCD a baja energía</cite>. Esto favorece a string respecto a GUT/punto-partícula.
- Contact interactions a escalas sub-Planck y KK gravitones: <cite id="5e4b3b04-0">Correcciones de contacto por debajo de Ms</cite><cite id="4a855975-2">Missing energy por gravitón real en extra-dimensiones vs</cite> <cite id="4a855975-2">resonancias de KK gauge sin contribución gravitaria dominante</cite>. Esto separa escenarios ADD/RS (con gravedad extra-dimensional) de ToEs sin dimensiones.
- Dinámica de agujeros negros vs string-balls: <cite id="4a855975-1">String balls decaen térmicamente</cite><cite id="4a855975-0">UMB para BH en TeV-string supera LHC</cite>, diferenciando string de otras ToEs con predicciones de BH primordiales directos.
- Objetos únicos de string: <cite id="5e4b3b04-2">Tensores antisimétricos con límites operativos en electron colliders</cite> y correlaciones gauge-gravedad únicas.
- Comparaciones entre construcciones string: <cite id="5e4b3b04-3">Tablas de distinguibilidad en observables LHC muestran “Yes/No/Probably” según el espacio de parámetros</cite>.

9) Limitaciones y planeamiento experimental
Aunque las diferencias son claras en teoría, la superposición de “árboles” (partículas adicionales) complica la separación pura y simple; por ello, <cite id="5e4b3b04-4">la estrategia práctica es combinar observables universales (p. ej., Reggeon amplitudes, módulo de invariant mass dijet y correlaciones gauge+fermión) con conteos en canales limpios (p. ej., Bhabha/Møller) que restringen sectores únicos de string</cite>. Los límites actuales de LHC en Ms y en tensores antisimétricos delimitan zonas de parámetros reales; <cite id="eb6a778e-0">para descubrir Regge strings a Ms ~ TeV, se requiere alta luminosidad y algoritmos sensibles a dijet subestructura y a picos estrechos</cite>, mientras que <cite id="eb6a778e-1">colisionadores de alta energía (100 TeV) extienden el alcance hasta Ms ~10–20 TeV</cite>.

Title: Constraints on antisymmetric tensor fields from Bhabha scattering
Snippet: String theory is still the most compelling framework for particle and gravitational physics beyond the Standard Model. As such, it behooves us to seek out all possible avenues to experimental tests of string theory, and the existence of fundamental antisymmetric tensor fields is a unique prediction of string theory that should be tested at future facilities.

Title: Z ' -gauge bosons as harbingers of low-mass strings
Snippet: In TeV-scale gravity scenarios where the SM is realized on the world-volume of D-branes the presence of fundamental strings can also be unearthed by searching for the effects of their vibrations. The particles that appear as the quanta of oscillating string modes are called Regge excitations and have squared masses quantized in units of M s = 1/ √ α ′ , where α ′ is the Regge slope parameter [37]. The leading contributions of Regge recurrences to certain processes at hadron colliders are universal. This is because the full-fledged string amplitudes which describe 2 → 2 parton scattering subprocesses involving four gauge bosons as well as those with two gauge bosons and two chiral matter fields are (to leading order in string coupling, but all orders in α ′ ) independent of the D-brane configuration, the geometry of the extra dimensions, and whether supersymmetry is broken or not. Therefore, the s-channel pole terms of the average square amplitudes contributing to dijet production can be obtained independent of the details of the compactification scheme [38]. For phenomenological purposes, the poles need to be softened to a Breit-Wigner form by obtaining and utilizing the corrcet total widths of the resonances [39]. After this is done, it is feasible to compute genuine string corrections to dijet signals at the LHC [40]. 9 The CMS Collaboration has searched for such narrow resonances in their dijet mass spectrum [43]. After operating for only few months, with merely 2.9 inverse picobarns of integrated luminosity, the LHC CMS experiment has ruled out M s < 2.5 TeV. Title: MINI-REVIEW ON COLLIDER SIGNATURES FOR EXTRA DIMENSIONS
Snippet: Recent advances in string theory have revolutionized particle phenomenology. Namely, the previously unreachable Planck, string, and grand unification scales (M Pl , M st , and M GUT , respectively) can be brought down to a TeV range through the existence of extra dimensions. There have been a number of ideas that can bring either the Planck, GUT, or string scale down to TeV region. One expects the low energy phenomenology of these new ideas or models can be tested at current and future collider experiments. 

In this talk, we review collider signatures for the following two models of extra dimensions: (i) the one proposed by Arkani-Hamed, Dimopoulos, and Dvali, 1 in which the standard model (SM) particles live on a 3-brane while the gravity is free to propagate in extra dimensions of very large size ( < ∼ 1 mm). This model was motivated by the fact that the effective Planck scale is brought down to TeV to solve the hierarchy problem. Collider signatures for this model can be divided into two types: (a) emission of real gravitons into extra dimensions and thus gives rise to missing energy signals, and (b) exchanges of virtual gravitons that frequently lead to enhancement of production of SM particles. (ii) The model proposed by Dienes et al. 2 and Pomarol et al. 3 that the SM gauge bosons are allowed to propagate in extra dimensions (whereas the gravity effect here is negligible.) This model has the merit of unifying the gauge couplings at a scale much lower than the usual GUT scale. Collider signatures for this model are due to the existence of the Kaluza-Klein (KK) states of γ, W , Z, and g bosons.

Title: Magnetic black holes with higher-order curvature and gauge corrections in even dimensions
Snippet: What is the description of a black hole in the quantum theory of gravity? The answer to this question is one of the ultimate goals of modern physics. String theory which is consistently formulated in higher dimensions is a promising candidate of a unified theory. In string theory, the extra dimensions are usually considered to be compactified, and as a result, the effect of string theory is negligible for large astrophysical black holes. However, in order to discuss the formation of tiny black holes in the upcoming Large Hadron Collider (LHC) or the final fate of an evaporating black hole by the Hawking radiation, the effect of string theory cannot be neglected. If the horizon size becomes comparable to the curvature radius of the compactified extra dimensions, the black hole effectively becomes higherdimensional. Although the non-perturbative aspects of string theory have been intensively investigated in recent years focusing on the conjecture of anti-de Sitter(AdS)/conformal field theory(CFT) correspondence [1], the full description of a black hole in string theory is still far from complete. 

Another possible approach to study the string effect is to study black holes in the low-energy classical theory. Higher-dimensional general relativity is realized as the lowest order in the Regge slope expansion of strings. Then, it is known that the higher-curvature terms appear as the next stringy compensation. Among five types of string theories, there appears the so-called Gauss-Bonnet term in the heterotic string case [2,3], which is a ghost-free and renormalizable combination of the quadratic curvature terms [4]. The active study of the Gauss-Bonnet black holes has its roots in the discovery of the spherically symmetric vacuum Boulware-Deser-Wheeler solution [5], which is the counterpart of the Tangherlini solution in general relativity [6]. However, in spite of the considerable progress in recent years on this subject, even the stationary axisymmetric rotating vacuum black-hole solution, namely the counterpart of the Myers-Perry solution in general relativity [7], has not been obtained yet. (See [8] for recent reviews.) 

Since gauge fields are fundamental in the standard model, black holes with gauge fields are also important from the viewpoint of string theory.

documents.title: Study of highly-excited string states at the Large Hadron Collider
documents.snippet: In TeV-scale gravity scenarios with large extra dimensions, black holes may be produced at future colliders. Good arguments have been made for why general relativistic black holes may be just out of reach of the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). However, in weakly coupled string theory, highly excited string states--string balls--could be produced at the LHC with high rates and decay thermally, not unlike general relativistic black holes. In this paper, we simulate and study string ball production and decay at the LHC. We specifically emphasize the experimentally detectable similarities and differences between string balls and general relativistic black holes at a TeV scale.

documents.title: MINI-REVIEW ON COLLIDER SIGNATURES FOR EXTRA DIMENSIONS
documents.snippet:
Recent advances in string theory have revolutionized particle phenomenology. Namely, the previously unreachable Planck, string, and grand unification scales (M Pl , M st , and M GUT , respectively) can be brought down to a TeV range through the existence of extra dimensions. There have been a number of ideas that can bring either the Planck, GUT, or string scale down to TeV region. One expects the low energy phenomenology of these new ideas or models can be tested at current and future collider experiments. 

In this talk, we review collider signatures for the following two models of extra dimensions: (i) the one proposed by Arkani-Hamed, Dimopoulos, and Dvali, 1 in which the standard model (SM) particles live on a 3-brane while the gravity is free to propagate in extra dimensions of very large size ( < ∼ 1 mm). This model was motivated by the fact that the effective Planck scale is brought down to TeV to solve the hierarchy problem. Collider signatures for this model can be divided into two types: (a) emission of real gravitons into extra dimensions and thus gives rise to missing energy signals, and (b) exchanges of virtual gravitons that frequently lead to enhancement of production of SM particles. (ii) The model proposed by Dienes et al. 2 and Pomarol et al. 3 that the SM gauge bosons are allowed to propagate in extra dimensions (whereas the gravity effect here is negligible.) This model has the merit of unifying the gauge couplings at a scale much lower than the usual GUT scale. Collider signatures for this model are due to the existence of the Kaluza-Klein (KK) states of γ, W , Z, and g bosons.

documents.snippet:
What is the description of a black hole in the quantum theory of gravity? The answer to this question is one of the ultimate goals of modern physics. String theory which is consistently formulated in higher dimensions is a promising candidate of a unified theory. In string theory, the extra dimensions are usually considered to be compactified, and as a result, the effect of string theory is negligible for large astrophysical black holes. However, in order to discuss the formation of tiny black holes in the upcoming Large Hadron Collider (LHC) or the final fate of an evaporating black hole by the Hawking radiation, the effect of string theory cannot be neglected. If the horizon size becomes comparable to the curvature radius of the compactified extra dimensions, the black hole effectively becomes higherdimensional. Although the non-perturbative aspects of string theory have been intensively investigated in recent years focusing on the conjecture of anti-de Sitter(AdS)/conformal field theory(CFT) correspondence [1], the full description of a black hole in string theory is still far from complete. 

Another possible approach to study the string effect is to study black holes in the low-energy classical theory. Higher-dimensional general relativity is realized as the lowest order in the Regge slope expansion of strings. Then, it is known that the higher-curvature terms appear as the next stringy compensation. Among five types of string theories, there appears the so-called Gauss-Bonnet term in the heterotic string case [2,3], which is a ghost-free and renormalizable combination of the quadratic curvature terms [4]. The active study of the Gauss-Bonnet black holes has its roots in the discovery of the spherically symmetric vacuum Boulware-Deser-Wheeler solution [5], which is the counterpart of the Tangherlini solution in general relativity [6]. However, in spite of the considerable progress in recent years on this subject, even the stationary axisymmetric rotating vacuum black-hole solution, namely the counterpart of the Myers-Perry solution in general relativity [7], has not been obtained yet. (See [8] for recent reviews.) 

Since gauge fields are fundamental in the standard model, black holes with gauge fields are also important from the viewpoint of string theory.
